rounds.text: Sprayking Ltd trades at a price-to-book ratio of 0.96x based on a share price of ₹ 1.37 against a book value of ₹ 1.42 [E2], and key ratios place the price-to-book even lower at 0.48x compared to a sector benchmark of 29.3x [E7]. This asset-backed valuation is deeply disconnected from the company's accelerating top-line expansion, highlighted by compounded sales growth of 24% over 5 years [E15] and surging to 40% over the last 3 years [E16]. This historical momentum is reinforced by recent fundamental screens capturing year-over-year sales spikes of 173% [E64] and robust annual profit growth exceeding 20% [E67]. Furthermore, the stock sits only 19% of the way up its 52-week range [E5], offering an entry point that completely ignores structural growth rates well above the sector median sales growth of 14.9% [E76]. Conceded: the trailing twelve months show a sales contraction of 15% [E17], and the return on assets of 3.29% lags far behind the sector benchmark of 25.48% [E8].

Sprayking Ltd trades at an alarming price-to-earnings ratio of 76.2x according to filed statements [E1], which signals an excessive valuation that the underlying fundamentals struggle to support. This lofty multiple is paired with a complete absence of shareholder return, as demonstrated by a dividend yield of 0.00% [E4]. Furthermore, operational efficiency lags severely behind industry peers, with a return on assets of just 3.29% compared to a sector benchmark of 25.48% [E8]. Compounded sales growth has also suffered a sharp reversal, plunging to -15% over the trailing twelve months [E17]. Compounding these concerns, recent price growth exceeds profit growth by 34%, indicating that market expectations are running dangerously ahead of actual business delivery [E55]. Conceded: the company maintains a low price-to-book ratio of 0.96x on a price of ₹ 1.37 against a book value of ₹ 1.42 [E2], alongside solid multi-year historical top-line expansion reaching 40% compounded over 3 years [E16].

The bull relies heavily on multi-year sales growth of 24% over 5 years [E15] and 40% over 3 years [E16], but ignores the severe growth reversal shown in the trailing twelve months where sales contracted by -15% [E17]. Conceded: historical compounded sales grew at 40% over 3 years [E16]. While the bull points to a low price-to-book ratio of 0.96x [E2] and positions the low 19% 52-week range placement [E5] as a cheap entry point, this discount is entirely justified by an abysmal return on assets of 3.29% that severely underperforms the sector benchmark of 25.48% [E8]. Furthermore, the premium valuation is highlighted by a lofty P/E ratio of 76.2 [E1], which directly contradicts the narrative of a uniformly cheap asset. The scanX signal engine confirms that expectations are running ahead of delivery, showing that price growth recently exceeds profit growth by 34% [E55]. Finally, the bull offers a 0.00% dividend yield [E4], providing no cash return to investors while they wait for fundamental delivery to catch up with the priced-in momentum.
